newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait sees 3.7 pct rise in oil revenue in 96/97.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait sees 3.7 pct rise in oil revenue in 96/97.

text.p: Kuwait on Saturday forecast a 3.7 percent rise in oil revenue to 3.859 billion dinars ($12.9 billion) in fiscal 1996/97 (June-July) from the previous year.
The Gulf Arab state's parliament on Saturday approved a budget by the Kuwait Oil Corp (KPC), the conglomorate which runs the country's oil sector.

Officials said the budget was calculated at a conservative weighted average barrel price of $13, unchanged from the past two years although world oil prices have averaged more than $3 a barrel higher so far this year.
KPC projected a 3.2 percent drop in revenue from crude oil sales to 1.729 billion dinars in 1996/97 and a nine percent rise from sales of oil by-products to 1.533 billion dinars.
It also expected a rise of 16 percent in revenue from sales of natural gas and liquefied gases.
Kuwait has a daily Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) quota of two million barrels.
